items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is short and clear, with sensible names (`fqdn`, `domain`) and the same try/encode('ascii')/except pattern already used in sanitize_address. Formatting matches the surrounding code. It is missing a comment on why message.py converts again, but that is a minor gap.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same `try: x.encode('ascii') except UnicodeEncodeError: x.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` block is pasted into both utils.get_fqdn and EmailMessage.message(), next to an existing copy in sanitize_address. There is no shared helper, and the message.py block is redundant once DNS_NAME is converted at its source.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It catches only the specific `UnicodeEncodeError`. Nothing is swallowed: if the idna conversion fails, the error is raised rather than hidden. ASCII hostnames pass through unchanged and there are no magic constants.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The conversion is done at the source in `CachedDnsName.get_fqdn`, so it works for every encoding and leaves ASCII hosts unchanged. But the idna logic is also repeated inline at the make_msgid call in message.py, so the same code exists in several places.
